title: GE4u Pharmacy English — Clinical Pharmacokinetics Module 01
disclaimer: For English-learning purposes only. Clinical examples require qualified pharmacist/physician review and current local product-information verification. Not a treatment or dosing protocol.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish Cmax, Tmax, AUC, Ctrough, clearance and half-life.
Explain enzyme inhibition versus induction using cautious scientific language.
Use specialist collocations in a clinical-pharmacy case discussion.
Identify when to escalate a suspected interaction rather than recommend an independent dose change.

terms.definition: Study of the time course of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion.
terms.example: The review compared the pharmacokinetic profiles of the two formulations.
terms.confusion: Do not confuse pharmacokinetics (what the body does to a drug) with pharmacodynamics (what the drug does to the body).

terms.vi: nồng độ đỉnh quan sát được
terms.definition: The maximum observed concentration in a specified sampling interval.
terms.example: The study reported a higher Cmax but did not establish a proportional increase in total exposure.
terms.confusion: Cmax is a concentration, not a time.

terms.vi: thời gian đạt nồng độ đỉnh
terms.definition: The time at which the observed maximum concentration occurs.
terms.example: A shorter Tmax may indicate more rapid absorption under the study conditions.
terms.confusion: Tmax describes timing; Cmax describes peak magnitude.

terms.vi: diện tích dưới đường cong nồng độ–thời gian
terms.definition: An integrated measure of drug exposure over a defined interval.
terms.example: AUC was used to compare systemic exposure over the prespecified interval.
terms.confusion: AUC and Cmax describe different aspects of exposure and are not interchangeable.

terms.definition: A concentration sampled near the end of a dosing interval, commonly immediately before the next dose when specified by the protocol.
terms.example: The clinical team interpreted the trough concentration alongside timing, adherence and the patient's clinical context.
terms.confusion: Sampling time matters; a level taken at the wrong time may be difficult to interpret.

terms.definition: The apparent volume of plasma cleared of drug per unit time.
terms.example: Reduced clearance can contribute to increased exposure, depending on the drug and circumstances.
terms.confusion: Clearance is a volume-per-time measure, not simply the amount of drug excreted.

terms.definition: The time required for the amount or concentration to decrease by half under the applicable kinetic conditions.
terms.example: A prolonged half-life may delay the time required to approach steady state.
terms.confusion: Half-life does not alone determine a safe dose or dosing interval.

terms.definition: A dynamic condition in which the average rate of drug input equals the average rate of drug elimination over a dosing interval.
terms.example: The sampling schedule was designed to assess concentrations at steady state.
terms.confusion: Steady state does not mean the concentration is constant at every moment.

terms.definition: A substance that reduces enzyme activity; for a susceptible substrate, inhibition may reduce metabolism and increase exposure.
terms.example: The team reviewed whether the newly prescribed medicine inhibits a pathway responsible for the substrate's metabolism.
terms.confusion: The direction and clinical size of an interaction depend on the specific drug and pathway.

terms.definition: A substance that increases enzyme expression or activity over time; a susceptible substrate may be metabolised more rapidly.
terms.example: The pharmacist considered whether induction could reduce exposure to the affected medicine.
terms.confusion: Induction may take time to develop and resolve; do not treat it as an immediate mirror image of inhibition.

terms.vi: theo dõi nồng độ thuốc trong điều trị
terms.definition: Measurement and interpretation of drug concentrations to support therapy where monitoring is appropriate.
terms.example: TDM results were interpreted with the sample time and clinical context documented.
terms.confusion: A measured concentration must be interpreted using drug-specific guidance, not in isolation.

case.title: Potential CYP3A interaction in a transplant recipient
case.scenario: A transplant recipient taking tacrolimus is prescribed clarithromycin. This is a high-risk interaction scenario used for language practice; consult current local product information and the transplant service's protocol.
case.model_response: This combination raises a clinically significant interaction concern because clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A-mediated metabolism and may increase tacrolimus exposure. I would promptly escalate the issue to the transplant team or clinical pharmacist and follow the approved monitoring protocol. I would not make an independent dose change.

quiz.q: Which measure integrates concentration over a defined time interval?
quiz.explanation: AUC represents integrated exposure over time. Tmax is a time measure and Cmax is the maximum observed concentration.

quiz.q: A strong inhibitor is added to a susceptible enzyme substrate. Which statement is most defensible?
quiz.explanation: Inhibition may reduce metabolism and increase exposure, but the actual magnitude and clinical outcome depend on the drug and patient.

quiz.q: Why is Ctrough not interchangeable with Cmax?
options: They are sampled/defined at different points in the concentration–time profile
Ctrough is a measure of time
quiz.answer: They are sampled/defined at different points in the concentration–time profile
quiz.explanation: Cmax describes the peak concentration; Ctrough is the concentration near the end of a dosing interval.

quiz.q: In the case, what is the appropriate learner response?
options: Ignore the interaction unless symptoms appear
Escalate promptly and follow approved monitoring guidance
quiz.answer: Escalate promptly and follow approved monitoring guidance
quiz.explanation: The exercise teaches communication and risk recognition, not independent prescribing.
